name: Maká (maca1260, ISO mca; Mataguayan, Paraguay)
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (0 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.recode_to: No change to the primary rule (fixed final, final stress). Flag for the compilers: Gerzenstein 1989:68 (as relayed by Nikulin & Carol 2024:234) gives weight-conditioned SECONDARY stress in words of 4+ syllables (peninitial if closed, else initial); the compilers note's IN-test 2 ('no syllable-internal makeup referenced at any stress level') is no longer literally true — decide whether the strict/quantity-insensitive register is defined on primary stress only; if it counts secondary stress, strict membership needs review.

sources.quote: 'According to Gerzenstein's (1989) description, Maká does not retain any traces of the prosodic distinctions that we reconstruct for Proto-Mataguayan. Instead, Maká has innovated an edge-demarcation pattern whereby the final syllable of a word receives primary stress' (exx. from Gerzenstein 1989:67-68: saˈlal 'cicada', salaˈlits 'cicadas', siˀwalaˈχits 'spiders', honokok'enˈxuʔ 'I kneel'). sources.quote: No stress statement: gives only the consonant/vowel inventory (Gerzenstein 1995a:41) and the practical alphabet; 'acento' occurs only in the idiom 'poner el acento en' and in a generic list of cross-linguistic compound criteria ('la presencia de un único acento', p. ~50) not applied to Maká.
